newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish meat firm Morliny eyes bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Polish meat firm Morliny eyes bourse listing.

text.p: Polish meat processing company Zaklady Przemyslu Miesnego Ostroda-Morliny SA plans to raise its capital in late 1997 and then enter the bourse's main market, the company's president said on Thursday.
"The capital increase will take place in October or in November 1997 at the latest, and our bourse debut is planned for late 1997 or early 1998," Miroslaw Szulc told Reuters.
He said the decision on the method and size of the capital increase would be taken at the end of May but that it would be made through a new share issue.
The share capital of Morliny, controlled by National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 15, amounts to 10.8 million zlotys and is divided into 5.25 million shares.
NFI 15 holds a 33-percent stake in the company, the remaining 14 funds have 27 percent, the treasury 25 percent, and 15 percent is held by its employees.
The company's gross profit was 11.5 million zlotys last year. No comparative financial results were immediately available.
